## Proof

**Claim.** The VC-dimension of $H_{n\text{-parity}}$ is $n$.

### Setup

Each $h_I$ is a linear functional over $\mathbb{F}_2^n$: identifying the indicator vector $a \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ of $I$ with the function, we have $h_I(x) = \langle a, x \rangle \pmod{2}$. The class $H_{n\text{-parity}}$ is exactly the set of all homogeneous linear forms on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, a vector space of dimension $n$ with $|H_{n\text{-parity}}| = 2^n$.

A set $S = \{x^{(1)}, \dots, x^{(d)}\} \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ is **shattered** iff for every labeling $\ell = (\ell_1,\dots,\ell_d) \in \{0,1\}^d$ there exists $I$ (equivalently $a \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$) such that
$$\langle a, x^{(j)}\rangle = \ell_j \pmod{2}, \quad j = 1,\dots,d.$$

Let $X \in \mathbb{F}_2^{d \times n}$ be the matrix whose $j$-th row is $x^{(j)}$. The shattering condition becomes: for every $\ell \in \mathbb{F}_2^d$, the system $Xa = \ell$ has a solution $a \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$. This holds **iff the linear map $a \mapsto Xa$ is surjective**, i.e. iff $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{F}_2}(X) = d$.

### Lower bound: $n$ points can be shattered

Take $S = \{e_1, e_2, \dots, e_n\}$, the standard basis vectors. Then $X = I_n$, which has rank $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$. For any desired labeling $\ell \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, choose $a = \ell$ (i.e. $I = \{i : \ell_i = 1\}$); then $\langle a, e_j \rangle = \ell_j$ for all $j$. Hence $S$ is shattered, so $\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{n\text{-parity}}) \geq n$.

### Upper bound: $n+1$ points cannot be shattered

For any set of $n+1$ points, the matrix $X \in \mathbb{F}_2^{(n+1) \times n}$ has rank at most $\min(n+1, n) = n < n+1$. Therefore the map $a \mapsto Xa$ is not surjective: there exists some $\ell \in \mathbb{F}_2^{n+1}$ not in the image, so no parity function realizes that labeling. Hence no set of $n+1$ points is shattered, giving $\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{n\text{-parity}}) \leq n$.

### Conclusion

Combining both bounds,

$$\boxed{\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{n\text{-parity}}) = n.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
